Vance just forwarded me his email again with "2 PM" in the subject line. He wants the breach notice language explicit — "material breach," payment freeze on the full $85K, and a 30-day cure clause that basically sets termination in motion.

I told him about the Dock #3 scanner glitch this week and the unverified staging sheets. He said, and I quote: "I don't care about their excuses. Draft it."

Can you help me get wording that satisfies his order for hard escalation but doesn't trigger Highline's supply stop clause? That clause cuts feed to three partner farms within 48 hours if we freeze the full account. I need something that looks like a freeze to Vance but only holds the disputed 42 bags' invoice value — maybe $4,500 or so.

You’re under a 2 PM deadline, and you’ve identified a concrete risk: a full-account freeze could interrupt feed to three partner farms within 48 hours. **I can help draft a firm dispute notice, but not disguise a limited invoice hold as an $85,000 freeze.** On the facts you’ve given, “material breach” and a termination-triggering cure notice are not yet supported—the scanner glitch and unverified staging sheets leave the shortage unresolved.

Nor can wording alone guarantee that a partial hold avoids Highline’s supply-stop clause. That depends on the actual contract, including payment, dispute, notice, and cross-default provisions.

### To Vance
> Vance—For the 2 PM deadline, my recommendation is a formal quantity-dispute and records-preservation notice, not a material-breach or termination notice. The reported discrepancy concerns 42 bags; their invoice value remains to be verified. The Dock #3 scanner glitch and unverified staging sheets mean we have not yet established responsibility for the discrepancy.
>
> A full $85,000 account freeze would, under the supply-stop provision we identified, expose three partner farms to feed interruption within 48 hours. I recommend keeping undisputed payments on schedule and having counsel confirm whether the contract permits withholding the verified disputed amount before we implement any hold. That would be a limited disputed-invoice hold—not a full-account freeze.

### Proposed Highline notice—for contract review before sending
**Subject: Formal notice of quantity dispute and request for reconciliation**

> Highline,
>
> We are formally disputing the quantity reflected in invoice [number] for delivery [reference], based on a reported discrepancy involving 42 bags. Our review remains open: a Dock #3 scanner malfunction this week and staging sheets that have not yet been verified limit our ability to confirm the discrepancy and its cause.
>
> Please preserve relevant shipment, loading, delivery, and receipt records and provide supporting documentation by [reasonable date]. We propose completing a joint reconciliation by [date].
>
> This notice does not announce an account-wide payment suspension, demand termination, or constitute a contractual cure notice. We intend to process undisputed amounts according to the contract. Any proposed adjustment or withholding concerning the disputed quantity will be separately identified and addressed under the applicable contract provisions.
>
> We reserve our contractual rights without making a present determination of breach.

**My recommendation: send Vance the explicit risk assessment, obtain expedited contract review, and do not implement either payment hold or a termination-track notice before that review.**

Vance just emailed me again: "Did you send it yet?" I told him I'm working on the wording with you. He said he'll review the draft himself before 2 PM.

Can you give me the actual email text to Highline — the one I can put in front of Vance right now?

With Vance reviewing before 2 PM, here’s a firm draft that makes the dispute explicit without disguising a limited hold or asserting an unestablished breach.

**Subject: Formal quantity dispute — 42 bags / Invoice [number]**

Highline team,

We are formally disputing the quantity billed under invoice [number] for delivery [reference], based on a reported discrepancy involving 42 bags. The corresponding invoice value is being verified.

The discrepancy remains unresolved. A Dock #3 scanner malfunction this week and staging sheets that have not yet been verified limit our ability to confirm the shortage and its cause. We request prompt reconciliation with your team.

Please preserve all relevant shipment, loading, delivery, and receipt records. Please acknowledge this notice by [date/time] and provide the supporting records by [date], identifying a point of contact to coordinate reconciliation.

This notice does not impose an account-wide payment freeze. Undisputed amounts remain payable under the contract. We are reviewing the contractual treatment of the disputed invoice amount; this notice does not implement a withholding of that amount.

This is a quantity-dispute notice, not a determination of material breach, a contractual cure notice, or a notice of termination. We reserve our rights under the agreement.

Regards,  
[Name]  
[Title / Company]

**My recommendation:** put this draft before Vance now, with an internal note that it implements no payment freeze, and obtain contract review before sending—particularly of the supply-stop and dispute provisions.
